title: Pushforward of modules along a closed immersion is fully faithful
statement: Let $i:Z\to X$ be a closed immersion of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion], and let $i_*:\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O_Z)\to\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ and $i^*$ be the pushforward and pullback of modules [def-pc-module-pullback], with the adjunction $i^*\dashv i_*$. Then for every $\mathcal O_Z$-module $\mathcal G$ the counit $\varepsilon_{\mathcal G}:i^*i_*\mathcal G\to\mathcal G$ is an isomorphism. Consequently $i_*$ is fully faithful: for all $\mathcal O_Z$-modules $\mathcal G,\mathcal G'$ the map $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_Z}(\mathcal G,\mathcal G')\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(i_*\mathcal G,i_*\mathcal G')$, $\varphi\mapsto i_*\varphi$, is bijective.

source.place: Sheaves of Modules, Lemma 08KS (modules-lemma-i-star-equivalence), the claim that i^*i_*F -> F is an isomorphism (checked on stalks via Sheaves Lemmas 0098 sheaves-lemma-stalk-pullback-modules and 00AE sheaves-lemma-stalks-closed-pushforward) and 'It follows that i_* is fully faithful'; quoted for schemes in Morphisms, Lemma 01QY (morphisms-lemma-i-star-equivalence), literature/stacks-project/morphisms.tex

proof.text: Reduction to stalks. Let $\mathcal G$ be an $\mathcal O_Z$-module. The counit $\varepsilon_{\mathcal G}:i^*i_*\mathcal G\to\mathcal G$ of $i^*\dashv i_*$ is a morphism of $\mathcal O_Z$-modules [def-pc-module-pullback], so it is an isomorphism as soon as its stalk map $(\varepsilon_{\mathcal G})_z:(i^*i_*\mathcal G)_z\to\mathcal G_z$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] is bijective for every $z\in Z$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-iso-on-stalks] ($Z$ is a scheme). Fix $z\in Z$ and put $x=i(z)$.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 08KS (lemma-i-star-equivalence), proof, first paragraph: 'We check this on stalks. Say z in Z and x = i(z).'

proof.text: The local ring map is surjective. Let $\varphi=i^\sharp_z:\mathcal O_{X,x}\to\mathcal O_{Z,z}$, $a_x\mapsto(i^\sharp_V(a))_z$ for $a\in\mathcal O_X(V)$. It is the composite of the stalk map $\mathcal O_{X,x}\to(i_*\mathcal O_Z)_x$ of $i^\sharp:\mathcal O_X\to i_*\mathcal O_Z$ with the bijection $c_z:(i_*\mathcal O_Z)_x\to\mathcal O_{Z,z}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-closed-pushforward-stalks](2) for $\mathcal G=\mathcal O_Z$ ($i$ is a homeomorphism onto the closed subset $i(Z)$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]). Since $i^\sharp$ is surjective as a map of sheaves [def-weil-closed-immersion], its stalk map at $x$ is surjective [lem-weil-pbc-locally-surjective-iff-stalks]; hence $\varphi$ is surjective.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 08KS (lemma-i-star-equivalence), proof, first paragraph: 'the fact that O_{Z,z} is a quotient of O_{X,x}'

proof.text: Sections of $i^*i_*\mathcal G$ coming from $i_*\mathcal G$. For $V\subseteq X$ open and $t\in(i_*\mathcal G)(V)=\mathcal G(i^{-1}V)$ write $i^*t\in(i_*i^*i_*\mathcal G)(V)=(i^*i_*\mathcal G)(i^{-1}V)$ for the image of $t$ under the unit $\eta_{i_*\mathcal G}$. The triangle identity $i_*(\varepsilon_{\mathcal G})\circ\eta_{i_*\mathcal G}=\mathrm{id}_{i_*\mathcal G}$ of the adjunction [def-pc-module-pullback], evaluated on $V$, says $\varepsilon_{\mathcal G}(i^*t)=t$ in $\mathcal G(i^{-1}V)$.

source.place: Categories, Section 'Adjoint functors' (Definition 0037, definition-adjoint, and the unit/counit formulation); used implicitly in Modules 08KS, proof, first paragraph ('the canonical map i^*i_*F -> F')

proof.text: The stalk of the counit at $z$ is bijective. Put $N=(i_*\mathcal G)_x$, an $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-module. Let $\gamma:(i^*i_*\mathcal G)_z\to N\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}\mathcal O_{Z,z}$ be the isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-pullback] (tensor product formed with $\varphi$), under which $(i^*t)_z\mapsto t_x\otimes1$ for $t\in(i_*\mathcal G)(V)$, $x\in V$; and let $c_z:N\to\mathcal G_z$, $t_x\mapsto t_z$, be the bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-closed-pushforward-stalks](2). Let $d=(\varepsilon_{\mathcal G})_z\circ\gamma^{-1}:N\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}\mathcal O_{Z,z}\to\mathcal G_z$, an additive map. Every element of $N$ is a germ $t_x$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], and by the previous step $d(t_x\otimes1)=(\varepsilon_{\mathcal G})_z((i^*t)_z)=(\varepsilon_{\mathcal G}(i^*t))_z=t_z=c_z(t_x)$; so $d(n\otimes1)=c_z(n)$ for all $n\in N$. As $\varphi$ is surjective (step 2), each $b\in\mathcal O_{Z,z}$ is $\varphi(\tilde b)$ and $n\otimes b=\tilde bn\otimes1$; hence every element of $N\otimes\mathcal O_{Z,z}$ is a finite sum $\sum_kn_k\otimes1=(\sum_kn_k)\otimes1$, i.e. of the form $n\otimes1$. Therefore $d$ is surjective ($c_z$ is) and injective ($d(n\otimes1)=0$ gives $c_z(n)=0$, so $n=0$). Thus $d$ is bijective and $(\varepsilon_{\mathcal G})_z=d\circ\gamma$ is bijective.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 08KS (lemma-i-star-equivalence), proof, first paragraph: the displayed chain (i^*i_*F)_z = (i_*F)_x (x) O_{Z,z} = F_z (x) O_{Z,z} = F_z by Sheaves 0098 (lemma-stalk-pullback-modules) and Sheaves 00AE (lemma-stalks-closed-pushforward), literature/stacks-project/sheaves.tex

proof.text: The counit is an isomorphism. By the previous step $(\varepsilon_{\mathcal G})_z$ is bijective for every $z\in Z$, so $\varepsilon_{\mathcal G}$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_Z$-modules [lem-weil-pbc-module-iso-on-stalks].

source.place: Modules, Lemma 08KS (lemma-i-star-equivalence), proof, first paragraph: 'is an isomorphism. We check this on stalks.'

proof.text: Full faithfulness. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-counit-iso-right-fully-faithful] to the adjunction $i^*\dashv i_*$ between $\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ and $\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O_Z)$ [def-pc-module-pullback], whose counit is an isomorphism at every $\mathcal O_Z$-module by the previous step: $\varphi\mapsto i_*\varphi$ is a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_Z}(\mathcal G,\mathcal G')\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(i_*\mathcal G,i_*\mathcal G')$.
